title: Lie Subgroups Actions and Homogeneous Spaces

items.title: Lie subalgebras and ideals
items.statement: For a finite-dimensional Lie algebra g, a linear subspace h is a Lie subalgebra when [h,h] is contained in h, and an ideal when [g,h] is contained in h.

references.title: Pavel Etingof, MIT 18.745 Lie Groups and Lie Algebras I
references.locator: Section 8.3, printed page 50

references.title: Alexander Kirillov Jr., An Introduction to Lie Groups and Lie Algebras
references.locator: Section 3.4, Definitions 3.43 and 3.46

items.title: Immersed, embedded, and closed Lie subgroups
items.statement: A Lie subgroup H of a Lie group G is an injectively immersed Lie group whose inclusion is a smooth homomorphism. Embedded means the inclusion is an embedding; closed means its image is closed in G.

references.title: John M. Lee, Introduction to Smooth Manifolds, 2nd ed.
references.locator: Chapter 7, Lie subgroups; Theorem 19.25, printed page 506

references.title: Pavel Etingof, MIT 18.745 Lie Groups and Lie Algebras I
references.locator: Definitions 3.10 and 4.5, printed pages 26 and 29

items.title: The Lie algebra of a Lie subgroup is a Lie subalgebra
items.statement: If i:H→G is a Lie subgroup inclusion, then di_e is injective and identifies Lie(H) with a Lie subalgebra of Lie(G).

references.title: John M. Lee, Introduction to Smooth Manifolds, 2nd ed.
references.locator: Definition 19.25 and the paragraph following it, printed page 506

references.title: Alexander Kirillov Jr., An Introduction to Lie Groups and Lie Algebras
references.locator: Proposition 3.12(1), printed page 32

items.title: Left-translated distribution associated to a Lie subalgebra
items.statement: Assume countable choice. For h⊆Lie(G), define D_g=dL_g(h)⊆T_gG. The tangent trivialization makes D a smooth constant-rank distribution.

references.title: John M. Lee, Introduction to Smooth Manifolds, 2nd ed.
references.locator: Equation (19.7) and Lemma 19.24, printed page 506

items.title: A Lie-subalgebra distribution is involutive
items.statement: Assume countable choice. The left-translated distribution D associated to a Lie subalgebra h is involutive.

references.title: John M. Lee, Introduction to Smooth Manifolds, 2nd ed.
references.locator: Lemma 19.24 and proof, printed page 506

items.title: Lie subgroup–Lie subalgebra correspondence
items.statement: Assume countable choice. Every Lie subalgebra h⊆Lie(G) is the Lie algebra of a unique connected immersed Lie subgroup H⊆G.

references.title: John M. Lee, Introduction to Smooth Manifolds, 2nd ed.
references.locator: Theorem 19.26 and proof, printed pages 506–507

references.title: Pavel Etingof, MIT 18.745 Lie Groups and Lie Algebras I
references.locator: Sections 9.3 and 10.2, printed pages 55 and 60–61

items.title: Connected Lie subgroups with the same Lie algebra are equal
items.statement: Assume countable choice. Two connected immersed Lie subgroups of G with the same tangent Lie subalgebra have the same image and intrinsic immersed subgroup structure.

references.title: John M. Lee, Introduction to Smooth Manifolds, 2nd ed.
references.locator: Uniqueness clause of Theorem 19.26, printed pages 506–507

items.title: An ideal integrates to a connected immersed normal subgroup
items.statement: Assume countable choice. The connected immersed subgroup integrating an ideal h of Lie(G) is normal in the identity component G⁰. It is normal in G if h is invariant under every Ad_g.

references.title: John M. Lee, Introduction to Smooth Manifolds, 2nd ed.
references.locator: Theorem 20.28 and proof, printed pages 535–536

references.title: Anthony W. Knapp, Lie Groups Beyond an Introduction, 2nd ed.
references.locator: Proposition 1.91 and the ideals/normal-subgroups discussion in Chapter I §10, printed pages 80–81

items.title: No small subgroups in a Lie group
items.statement: Every Lie group G has an identity neighbourhood containing no subgroup other than {e}.

references.title: John M. Lee, Introduction to Smooth Manifolds, 2nd ed.
references.locator: Lie-group multiplication and exponential-chart discussion in Chapter 20, especially Proposition 20.8, printed pages 519–521

items.title: Cartan closed subgroup theorem
items.statement: Every closed subgroup H of a finite-dimensional Lie group G has a unique smooth structure making it an embedded Lie subgroup.

references.title: John M. Lee, Introduction to Smooth Manifolds, 2nd ed.
references.locator: Theorem 20.12 and complete proof, printed pages 523–525

references.title: Anthony W. Knapp, Lie Groups Beyond an Introduction, 2nd ed.
references.locator: Chapter I §10, quotient and closed-subgroup discussion, printed page 77

items.title: Discrete subgroups are closed embedded zero-dimensional Lie subgroups
items.statement: A subgroup Γ of a Lie group is discrete exactly when it is a closed embedded zero-dimensional Lie subgroup.

references.title: John M. Lee, Introduction to Smooth Manifolds, 2nd ed.
references.locator: Proposition 21.28 and complete proof, printed page 556

items.title: Continuous homomorphisms between Lie groups are smooth
items.statement: Every continuous group homomorphism F:G→H between finite-dimensional Lie groups is smooth.

references.title: Anthony W. Knapp, Lie Groups Beyond an Introduction, 2nd ed.
references.locator: Chapter I §10, automatic smoothness statement and canonical-coordinate route, printed page 77

references.title: John M. Lee, Introduction to Smooth Manifolds, 2nd ed.
references.locator: Closed Subgroup Theorem 20.12, printed pages 523–525

items.title: Lie group homomorphisms have constant rank
items.statement: A smooth Lie group homomorphism F:G→H has rank equal to rank(dF_e) at every point.

references.title: John M. Lee, Introduction to Smooth Manifolds, 2nd ed.
references.locator: First Isomorphism Theorem discussion, printed page 556

references.title: Pavel Etingof, MIT 18.745 Lie Groups and Lie Algebras I
references.locator: Proposition 4.7 and proof in Section 9.1, printed pages 29 and 53–54

items.title: Kernels are closed embedded normal Lie subgroups
items.statement: For a smooth Lie group homomorphism F:G→H, ker F is a closed embedded normal Lie subgroup and Lie(ker F)=ker(dF_e).

references.title: John M. Lee, Introduction to Smooth Manifolds, 2nd ed.
references.locator: Theorem 21.27 and proof, printed page 556

references.title: Pavel Etingof, MIT 18.745 Lie Groups and Lie Algebras I
references.locator: Corollary 9.5 and proof, printed pages 53–54

items.title: Images are immersed Lie subgroups
items.statement: The image of a smooth Lie group homomorphism F:G→H has a unique immersed subgroup structure for which the corestriction from G is a surjective submersion; its Lie algebra is im(dF_e). It need not be embedded.

references.title: John M. Lee, Introduction to Smooth Manifolds, 2nd ed.
references.locator: Theorem 21.27 and proof, printed page 556

references.title: Pavel Etingof, MIT 18.745 Lie Groups and Lie Algebras I
references.locator: Proposition 4.7 and Corollary 9.5, printed pages 29 and 53–54

items.title: First-isomorphism factorization for Lie group homomorphisms
items.statement: Every smooth F:G→H factors as a surjective submersion G→im F followed by the injective immersed-subgroup inclusion im F→H; algebraically, the fibres are the cosets of ker F.

references.title: John M. Lee, Introduction to Smooth Manifolds, 2nd ed.
references.locator: Theorem 21.27 and complete proof, printed page 556

references.title: Pavel Etingof, MIT 18.745 Lie Groups and Lie Algebras I
references.locator: Proposition 4.7 and Corollary 9.5, printed pages 29 and 53–54

items.title: Smooth left actions of Lie groups
items.statement: A smooth left action is a smooth map G×M→M with e·x=x and (gh)·x=g·(h·x).

references.title: Pavel Etingof, MIT 18.745 Lie Groups and Lie Algebras I
references.locator: Definition 4.8, printed page 30

references.title: John M. Lee, Introduction to Smooth Manifolds, 2nd ed.
references.locator: Chapter 21 opening conventions, printed page 541

items.title: Homogeneous spaces
items.statement: A homogeneous G-space is a smooth manifold with a smooth transitive left G-action. For a subgroup H, G/H denotes left cosets with the left translation action; a manifold structure is asserted only when H is closed.

references.title: John M. Lee, Introduction to Smooth Manifolds, 2nd ed.
references.locator: Homogeneous Spaces, printed pages 550–551

references.title: Pavel Etingof, MIT 18.745 Lie Groups and Lie Algebras I
references.locator: Section 4.1, printed page 28

items.title: Quotient manifold by a closed Lie subgroup
items.statement: Assuming AC_ω, if H is a closed subgroup of a finite-dimensional real Lie group G, then G/H has a unique smooth manifold structure for which q:G→G/H is a surjective submersion and the left G-action is smooth; dim(G/H)=dim G−dim H.

references.title: John M. Lee, Introduction to Smooth Manifolds, 2nd ed.
references.locator: Homogeneous Space Construction Theorem 21.17 and complete proof, printed pages 551–552

references.title: Pavel Etingof, MIT 18.745 Lie Groups and Lie Algebras I
references.locator: Theorem 4.1 and quotient-chart construction, printed page 28

items.title: The smooth structure on G/H is independent of the local complement
items.statement: Two finite-dimensional complements used in the quotient construction yield smoothly compatible quotient charts.

references.title: John M. Lee, Introduction to Smooth Manifolds, 2nd ed.
references.locator: Homogeneous Space Construction Theorem 21.17, quotient-chart compatibility argument, printed pages 551–552

items.title: Tangent space of a homogeneous quotient
items.statement: For closed H⊆G, dq_e induces a canonical linear isomorphism g/h≅T_{eH}(G/H), transported by left translation to every coset.

references.title: Pavel Etingof, MIT 18.745 Lie Groups and Lie Algebras I
references.locator: Theorem 4.1 and quotient tangent calculation, printed page 28

items.title: The isotropy action on G/H is induced by Ad modulo h
items.statement: For h∈H, the differential at eH of left multiplication by h corresponds under g/h≅T_{eH}(G/H) to X+h↦Ad_h X+h.

references.title: Pavel Etingof, MIT 18.745 Lie Groups and Lie Algebras I
references.locator: Homogeneous spaces and adjoint action, §§4.1 and 9.1, printed pages 28 and 53

items.title: Quotient by a closed normal subgroup is a Lie group
items.statement: If N is a closed normal Lie subgroup of G, the quotient manifold G/N has unique Lie-group operations making q a smooth homomorphism, and Lie(G/N)≅g/n.
items.strategy: Descend the group laws through the quotient, use local sections for smoothness, prove the tangent kernel is an ideal, define and check the quotient bracket directly, then identify it with the bracket on Lie(G/N).

references.title: John M. Lee, Introduction to Smooth Manifolds, 2nd ed.
references.locator: Quotient Group Theorem 21.26 and complete proof, printed pages 555–556

references.title: Pavel Etingof, MIT 18.745 Lie Groups and Lie Algebras I
references.locator: Proposition 4.7, printed page 29

items.title: The principal bundle G→G/H
items.statement: For closed H⊆G, q:G→G/H with right action g·h=gh is the canonical principal H-bundle candidate; local trivializations must be H-equivariant and use the convention (x,h)·k=(x,hk).

references.title: John M. Lee, Introduction to Smooth Manifolds, 2nd ed.
references.locator: Homogeneous Space Construction Theorem 21.17, printed pages 551–552

items.title: G→G/H is a smooth principal H-bundle
items.statement: For closed H⊆G, q:G→G/H is locally H-equivariantly diffeomorphic to U×H and hence is a smooth principal H-bundle.

references.title: John M. Lee, Introduction to Smooth Manifolds, 2nd ed.
references.locator: Homogeneous Space Construction Theorem 21.17 and local-product proof, printed pages 551–552

references.title: Pavel Etingof, MIT 18.745 Lie Groups and Lie Algebras I
references.locator: Theorem 4.1, printed page 28

items.title: Associated bundles
items.statement: For a right principal H-bundle P→M and a left representation ρ:H→GL(V), define P×_H V=(P×V)/((p,v)·h=(ph,ρ(h)^{-1}v)).

references.title: John M. Lee, Introduction to Smooth Manifolds, 2nd ed.
references.locator: Vector-bundle and fibre-bundle conventions, Chapter 10, especially printed pages 249–250 and 267–268

items.title: Associated vector bundles are well-defined
items.statement: The associated quotient P×_H V has a unique smooth rank-dim(V) vector-bundle structure over M, with local trivializations induced by principal-bundle sections and transition functions ρ(g_{ij}).

references.title: John M. Lee, Introduction to Smooth Manifolds, 2nd ed.
references.locator: Vector Bundle Chart Lemma 10.6 and complete proof, printed pages 252–253; fibre-bundle conventions, printed pages 267–268

items.title: Fundamental vector fields for a left action
items.statement: For a smooth left action and X∈g, define X_M(x)=d/dt|0 exp(−tX)·x. The minus sign is the standing convention.

references.title: John M. Lee, Introduction to Smooth Manifolds, 2nd ed.
references.locator: Equation (20.11) and Theorem 20.18, printed pages 529–530; sign translated to the standing convention

items.title: Fundamental vector fields form a Lie-algebra homomorphism
items.statement: With X_M(x)=d/dt|0 exp(−tX)·x, one has [X_M,Y_M]=[X,Y]_M.

references.title: John M. Lee, Introduction to Smooth Manifolds, 2nd ed.
references.locator: Theorem 20.18 and complete proof, printed pages 529–530; signs translated to the exp(-tX) convention

references.title: Pavel Etingof, MIT 18.745 Lie Groups and Lie Algebras I
references.locator: Proposition 9.1 and proof, printed page 53; opposite convention translated explicitly

items.title: Orbits, stabilizers, and orbit maps
items.statement: For x∈M define G_x={g:g·x=x}, G·x={g·x:g∈G}, and Φ_x:G→M by Φ_x(g)=g·x.

references.title: Pavel Etingof, MIT 18.745 Lie Groups and Lie Algebras I
references.locator: Section 4.4, printed page 31

references.title: John M. Lee, Introduction to Smooth Manifolds, 2nd ed.
references.locator: Quotients of Manifolds by Group Actions, printed page 541

items.title: Stabilizers are closed embedded Lie subgroups
items.statement: For a smooth action on a Hausdorff manifold, every stabilizer G_x is a closed embedded Lie subgroup.

references.title: John M. Lee, Introduction to Smooth Manifolds, 2nd ed.
references.locator: Stabilizer discussion and Closed Subgroup Theorem application, printed pages 541 and 551

references.title: Pavel Etingof, MIT 18.745 Lie Groups and Lie Algebras I
references.locator: Definition 4.5 and Proposition 4.7, printed page 29

items.title: Kernel of the infinitesimal orbit map
items.statement: The linear map g→T_xM, X↦X_M(x), has kernel Lie(G_x); its image is the tangent space of the immersed orbit.

references.title: Pavel Etingof, MIT 18.745 Lie Groups and Lie Algebras I
references.locator: Proposition 4.12 and Corollary 4.13, printed page 31

references.title: John M. Lee, Introduction to Smooth Manifolds, 2nd ed.
references.locator: Theorem 21.18 and proof, printed pages 552-553

items.title: Every orbit is an injectively immersed homogeneous space
items.statement: For a smooth G-action and x∈M, G/G_x maps G-equivariantly and injectively immersively onto G·x; this gives every orbit its canonical immersed homogeneous-space structure.

references.title: John M. Lee, Introduction to Smooth Manifolds, 2nd ed.
references.locator: Homogeneous Space Characterization Theorem 21.18 and proof, printed pages 552-553

references.title: Pavel Etingof, MIT 18.745 Lie Groups and Lie Algebras I
references.locator: Proposition 4.12 and Corollary 4.13, printed page 31

items.title: Transitive actions identify M with G/H
items.statement: If a smooth action is transitive, the orbit map induces a G-equivariant diffeomorphism G/G_x→M.

references.title: John M. Lee, Introduction to Smooth Manifolds, 2nd ed.
references.locator: Homogeneous Space Characterization Theorem 21.18 and complete proof, printed pages 552–553; Equivariant Rank Theorem 7.25, printed pages 165–166

references.title: Pavel Etingof, MIT 18.745 Lie Groups and Lie Algebras I
references.locator: Proposition 4.12 and proof, printed pages 30–31

items.title: Free and proper Lie-group actions
items.statement: An action is free if every stabilizer is trivial. It is proper if (g,x)↦(g·x,x) from G×M to M×M has compact inverse images of compact subsets.

references.title: John M. Lee, Introduction to Smooth Manifolds, 2nd ed.
references.locator: Definitions and discussion preceding Proposition 21.4, printed pages 542–543

items.title: Compact Lie-group actions are proper
items.statement: Every continuous action of a compact Lie group on a Hausdorff locally compact manifold is proper.

references.title: John M. Lee, Introduction to Smooth Manifolds, 2nd ed.
references.locator: Corollary 21.6 and proof, printed page 544

items.title: Local slice for a free proper action
items.statement: For a smooth free proper G-action and x∈M there is a submanifold slice S through x such that G×S→M is a diffeomorphism from a neighbourhood of (e,x) onto a neighbourhood of x, and sufficiently small translates meet only as forced by the identity neighbourhood.

references.title: John M. Lee, Introduction to Smooth Manifolds, 2nd ed.
references.locator: Proposition 21.5 and proof, printed pages 543–544; slice construction in Theorem 21.10, printed pages 545–547

items.title: Free proper action quotient manifold
items.statement: For a smooth free proper action of G on M, M/G is a Hausdorff second-countable smooth manifold of dimension dim M−dim G, and q:M→M/G is a surjective submersion.

references.title: John M. Lee, Introduction to Smooth Manifolds, 2nd ed.
references.locator: Proposition 21.4 and Theorem 21.10 with proofs, printed pages 543–547

items.title: A free proper action makes M→M/G a principal bundle
items.statement: For a free proper left action, q:M→M/G is a principal G-bundle after using the equivalent right action x·g=g^{-1}·x.

references.title: John M. Lee, Introduction to Smooth Manifolds, 2nd ed.
references.locator: Local product and quotient-chart construction in Theorem 21.10, printed pages 545–547

items.title: Tangent space of a free proper quotient
items.statement: For a free proper action, ker(dq_x) is the tangent space to G·x, and dq_x induces T_xM/T_x(G·x)≅T_[x](M/G).

references.title: John M. Lee, Introduction to Smooth Manifolds, 2nd ed.
references.locator: Product and quotient coordinates in Theorem 21.10, printed pages 545–547

items.title: Equivariant maps and equivariant vector bundles
items.statement: A map f:X→Y between G-spaces is equivariant when f(gx)=gf(x). A G-equivariant vector bundle E→M has a smooth G-action by fibrewise-linear bundle maps covering the action on M.

references.title: John M. Lee, Introduction to Smooth Manifolds, 2nd ed.
references.locator: Homogeneous Space Characterization Theorem 21.18, printed pages 552–553

items.title: Equivariant maps descend on free proper quotients
items.statement: An equivariant smooth map between free proper G-manifolds induces a unique smooth map on orbit quotients.

references.title: John M. Lee, Introduction to Smooth Manifolds, 2nd ed.
references.locator: Quotient-map smoothness criterion used in Theorem 21.10, printed pages 544–547

items.title: Covering homomorphisms of Lie groups
items.statement: A covering homomorphism is a smooth Lie-group homomorphism p:G̃→G whose underlying map is a covering map.

references.title: Pavel Etingof, MIT 18.745 Lie Groups and Lie Algebras I
references.locator: Section 3.2 and Proposition 3.5, printed pages 25–26

items.title: Connected covers of smooth manifolds have a canonical smooth structure
items.statement: If p:E→M is a covering map, M is a smooth manifold, and E is connected, then the given topological space E has a unique smooth structure for which p is a smooth local diffeomorphism; dim E=dim M.

references.title: Pavel Etingof, MIT 18.745 Lie Groups and Lie Algebras I
references.locator: Section 3.2 and Proposition 3.5, printed pages 25–26

references.title: John M. Lee, Introduction to Smooth Manifolds, 2nd ed.
references.locator: Smooth covering maps, Chapter 4; covering Lie groups, Theorem 21.32, printed page 558

items.title: Connected covers of connected Lie groups lift uniquely to Lie groups
items.statement: Let p:G̃→G be a connected covering of a connected Lie group and choose ẽ over e. There is a unique Lie-group structure on G̃ with identity ẽ for which p is a covering homomorphism.

references.title: Pavel Etingof, MIT 18.745 Lie Groups and Lie Algebras I
references.locator: Proposition 3.5 and proof, printed page 26

items.title: Universal covering Lie group
items.statement: Every connected Lie group G has a simply connected Lie group G̃ and a covering homomorphism G̃→G, unique up to a unique basepoint-preserving Lie-group isomorphism.

references.title: John M. Lee, Introduction to Smooth Manifolds, 2nd ed.
references.locator: Theorem 21.32, printed page 558

references.title: Pavel Etingof, MIT 18.745 Lie Groups and Lie Algebras I
references.locator: Proposition 3.5 and Corollary 3.6, printed page 26

items.title: The fundamental group of a connected Lie group is abelian
items.statement: For every connected Lie group G, π1(G,e) is abelian.

references.title: Pavel Etingof, MIT 18.745 Lie Groups and Lie Algebras I
references.locator: Proposition 3.5(ii) and Remark 3.7, printed page 26

items.title: Not every Lie subgroup is embedded and closed
items.statement: Every Lie subgroup is an embedded closed subset of its ambient Lie group.

references.title: John M. Lee, Introduction to Smooth Manifolds, 2nd ed.
references.locator: Example 21.3, printed page 542; immersed subgroup convention in Section 19.4

references.title: Pavel Etingof, MIT 18.745 Lie Groups and Lie Algebras I
references.locator: Definition 4.5 and Proposition 4.7, printed page 30

items.title: A Lie subalgebra need not integrate to a closed subgroup
items.statement: Every Lie subalgebra integrates to a closed Lie subgroup.

references.title: John M. Lee, Introduction to Smooth Manifolds, 2nd ed.
references.locator: Lie subgroup–subalgebra theorem, Theorem 19.26, printed pages 506–507; irrational torus flow, Example 21.3, printed page 542

references.title: Pavel Etingof, MIT 18.745 Lie Groups and Lie Algebras I
references.locator: Lie subgroups and subalgebras, Proposition 4.7, printed page 30

items.title: The irrational torus flow is free with dense orbits
items.statement: For irrational α, t·(z,w)=(exp(2πit)z,exp(2πiαt)w) is a smooth free R-action on T² with every orbit dense, and its orbit map at (1,1) is an injective immersed Lie-group homomorphism.

references.title: John M. Lee, Introduction to Smooth Manifolds, 2nd ed.
references.locator: Example 21.3, printed page 542

references.title: Pavel Etingof, MIT 18.745 Lie Groups and Lie Algebras I
references.locator: Irrational torus winding, Example 3.14(2), printed page 26; immersed-subgroup Example 4.6(1), printed page 29

items.title: A homomorphism image need not be embedded
items.statement: The image of every Lie-group homomorphism is an embedded Lie subgroup.

references.title: John M. Lee, Introduction to Smooth Manifolds, 2nd ed.
references.locator: Example 21.3, printed page 542

references.title: Pavel Etingof, MIT 18.745 Lie Groups and Lie Algebras I
references.locator: Irrational winding Examples 3.14(2) and 4.6(1), printed pages 26 and 29

items.title: G/H need not be a quotient Lie group
items.statement: For every closed subgroup H, the homogeneous space G/H has a Lie-group structure making the quotient map a homomorphism.

references.title: John M. Lee, Introduction to Smooth Manifolds, 2nd ed.
references.locator: Quotient Group Theorem 21.26 and complete proof, printed pages 555-556

references.title: Pavel Etingof, MIT 18.745 Lie Groups and Lie Algebras I
references.locator: Theorem 4.1 and Proposition 4.7, printed pages 28-29

items.title: A free action need not have a manifold quotient
items.statement: Every free smooth Lie-group action has a manifold orbit space.

references.title: John M. Lee, Introduction to Smooth Manifolds, 2nd ed.
references.locator: Example 21.3, printed page 542; Theorem 21.10, printed pages 544–547

items.title: The plus exponential convention is not a homomorphism for left actions
items.statement: For a left action, X↦(d/dt)|0 exp(tX)·x is a Lie-algebra homomorphism.

references.title: John M. Lee, Introduction to Smooth Manifolds, 2nd ed.
references.locator: Equation (20.11) and Theorem 20.18(a), including the sign computation in the complete proof, printed pages 529-530

references.title: Pavel Etingof, MIT 18.745 Lie Groups and Lie Algebras I
references.locator: Proposition 9.1 and proof, printed page 53

title: Lie Subgroups Actions and Homogeneous Spaces — Examples

items.title: An irrational line as a dense immersed Lie subgroup of a torus
items.statement: For irrational α, t↦(e^{2πit},e^{2πiαt}) injects R as a dense immersed nonembedded subgroup of T².

references.title: John M. Lee, Introduction to Smooth Manifolds, 2nd ed.
references.locator: Example 21.3, printed page 542; Lie Group Homomorphism Theorem 21.27 and following discussion, printed pages 556-557

references.title: Pavel Etingof, MIT 18.745 Lie Groups and Lie Algebras I
references.locator: Examples 3.14(2) and 4.6(1), printed pages 26 and 29

items.title: SL(n) as a closed Lie subgroup of GL(n)
items.statement: SL(n,F)=ker(det:GL(n,F)→F×) is a closed embedded Lie subgroup with Lie algebra the trace-zero matrices.

references.title: John M. Lee, Introduction to Smooth Manifolds, 2nd ed.
references.locator: Example 7.18(c),(e), printed pages 158–159; Lie Group Homomorphism Theorem 21.27, printed page 556

references.title: Pavel Etingof, MIT 18.745 Lie Groups and Lie Algebras I
references.locator: Examples 3.2-3.3, printed pages 25-26; Corollary 9.5, printed pages 53-54

items.title: Kernel and image of determinant
items.statement: For real GL(n), determinant has kernel SL(n) and image R×; on GL⁺(n) its image is R_{>0}, illustrating the Lie-group first isomorphism factorization.

references.title: John M. Lee, Introduction to Smooth Manifolds, 2nd ed.
references.locator: Examples 7.3(b) and 7.18(c), printed pages 153 and 158; Lie Group Homomorphism Theorem 21.27, printed page 556

references.title: Pavel Etingof, MIT 18.745 Lie Groups and Lie Algebras I
references.locator: Matrix-group examples, printed pages 23–25, and Corollary 9.5, printed pages 53–54

items.title: Spheres as SO(n+1)/SO(n)
items.statement: SO(n+1) acts transitively on S^n and the stabilizer of the last basis vector is SO(n), hence S^n≅SO(n+1)/SO(n) for n≥1.

references.title: John M. Lee, Introduction to Smooth Manifolds, 2nd ed.
references.locator: Examples following Homogeneous Space Characterization Theorem 21.18, especially sphere example, printed page 553

references.title: Pavel Etingof, MIT 18.745 Lie Groups and Lie Algebras I
references.locator: Example 4.17(1), printed page 31

items.title: Projective spaces as homogeneous spaces
items.statement: RP^n≅SO(n+1)/S(O(1)×O(n)) and CP^n≅U(n+1)/(U(1)×U(n)) as smooth homogeneous spaces.

references.title: John M. Lee, Introduction to Smooth Manifolds, 2nd ed.
references.locator: Homogeneous-space examples and Problem 21-10, printed pages 553 and 561

references.title: Pavel Etingof, MIT 18.745 Lie Groups and Lie Algebras I
references.locator: Homogeneous-space examples, Section 4, printed pages 29–31

items.title: Grassmannians and flag manifolds as homogeneous spaces
items.statement: Orthogonal or unitary groups act transitively on Grassmannians and flag manifolds, whose stabilizers are the corresponding block subgroups.

references.title: John M. Lee, Introduction to Smooth Manifolds, 2nd ed.
references.locator: Examples 21.21–21.22 and complete homogeneous-space calculations, printed pages 554–555

references.title: Pavel Etingof, MIT 18.745 Lie Groups and Lie Algebras I
references.locator: Flag-manifold discussion in Section 4, printed pages 31–32

items.title: SU(2)→SO(3) as a covering homomorphism
items.statement: Conjugation on imaginary quaternions gives a surjective covering homomorphism SU(2)→SO(3) with kernel {±1}.

references.title: Pavel Etingof, MIT 18.745 Lie Groups and Lie Algebras I
references.locator: Exercise 3.9 and both parts, printed page 26; Proposition 6.7 and proof, printed page 40

references.title: Anthony W. Knapp, Lie Groups Beyond an Introduction, 2nd ed.
references.locator: Introduction, Problems 6-9, printed pages 20-21

items.title: The Möbius line bundle as an associated bundle
items.statement: The sign representation of Z/2 acting on R associates to S¹→S¹, z↦z², the Möbius real line bundle.

references.title: John M. Lee, Introduction to Smooth Manifolds, 2nd ed.
references.locator: Möbius Bundle Example 10.3, printed pages 251–252, and Problem 21-9, printed pages 560–561

items.title: Integer translations on the line
items.statement: The action of Z on R by n·x=x+n is free and proper; R/Z is diffeomorphic to S¹ and R→S¹ is a principal Z-bundle.

references.title: John M. Lee, Introduction to Smooth Manifolds, 2nd ed.
references.locator: Discrete-group quotient discussion following Theorem 21.29, printed page 557; principal-bundle construction in Theorem 21.10, printed pages 545–547

references.title: Pavel Etingof, MIT 18.745 Lie Groups and Lie Algebras I
references.locator: Covering Lie groups, Proposition 3.5 and Example 3.7, printed pages 26–27

items.title: A free irrational torus action that is not proper
items.statement: For irrational α, t·(z,w)=(e^{2πit}z,e^{2πiαt}w) is a free smooth R-action on T² but is not proper and has a non-Hausdorff orbit quotient.

references.title: John M. Lee, Introduction to Smooth Manifolds, 2nd ed.
references.locator: Example 21.3, printed page 542

items.title: A proper nonfree action is not a principal bundle
items.statement: The rotation action of compact SO(2) on R² is proper but has stabilizer SO(2) at the origin, so R²→R²/SO(2) is not a principal SO(2)-bundle.

references.title: John M. Lee, Introduction to Smooth Manifolds, 2nd ed.
references.locator: Example 21.2(e), printed pages 541–542; Corollary 21.6, printed page 544

items.title: The tangent bundle of G/H as an associated bundle
items.statement: For closed H⊆G, T(G/H)≅G×_H(g/h), where H acts through Ad modulo h.

references.title: Pavel Etingof, MIT 18.745 Lie Groups and Lie Algebras I
references.locator: Homogeneous-space quotient and isotropy representation, Sections 4 and 9, printed pages 28–31 and 53

references.title: John M. Lee, Introduction to Smooth Manifolds, 2nd ed.
references.locator: Homogeneous Space Construction and Characterization Theorems 21.17–21.18, printed pages 551–553

title: Lie Algebra Representations Enveloping Algebras and Pbw

items.title: Lie algebras over a field
items.statement: A Lie algebra over a field k is a k-vector space g with a bilinear alternating bracket satisfying Jacobi. No finite-dimensional hypothesis is imposed.

references.title: Etingof, MIT 18.745 notes, §§3.2 and 11.1
Kirillov, An Introduction to Lie Groups and Lie Algebras, §§3.4 and 4.1

items.title: Lie subalgebras, ideals, and center
items.statement: A linear subspace h of g is a Lie subalgebra if [h,h]⊆h, an ideal if [g,h]⊆h, and Z(g)={z:[z,g]=0}.

references.title: Etingof, MIT 18.745 notes, §3.2
Kirillov, An Introduction to Lie Groups and Lie Algebras, §5.3

items.title: The quotient Lie-algebra bracket is well-defined
items.statement: If i is an ideal of g, [x+i,y+i]=[x,y]+i is independent of representatives and satisfies the Lie identities.

references.title: Kirillov, An Introduction to Lie Groups and Lie Algebras, §5.3, before Lemma 5.17

items.title: Quotient Lie algebras
items.statement: For an ideal i⊲g, the quotient vector space g/i with the bracket justified by the preceding lemma is the quotient Lie algebra.

references.title: Kirillov, An Introduction to Lie Groups and Lie Algebras, §5.3, before Lemma 5.17

items.title: Homomorphisms of possibly infinite-dimensional Lie algebras
items.statement: For Lie algebras g,h over the same field, with no dimension restriction, a homomorphism f:g→h is a linear map satisfying f([x,y])=[f(x),f(y)].

references.title: Etingof, MIT 18.745 notes, §3.2

items.title: Kernels, images, and the first isomorphism theorem for Lie algebras
items.statement: For a Lie-algebra homomorphism f:g→h, ker f is an ideal, im f a subalgebra, and g/ker f≅im f as Lie algebras.

references.title: Kirillov, An Introduction to Lie Groups and Lie Algebras, Lemma 5.17

items.title: Direct products and direct sums of Lie algebras
items.statement: Products carry the componentwise bracket; the algebraic direct sum is the finite-support subalgebra of the product.

references.title: Etingof, MIT 18.745 notes, componentwise direct-sum convention in §3

items.title: Derivations of Lie algebras
items.statement: A derivation D:g→g is linear and satisfies D[x,y]=[Dx,y]+[x,Dy].

references.title: Etingof, MIT 18.745 notes, derivations in §3.2

items.title: Derivations form a Lie algebra and inner derivations an ideal
items.statement: Der(g) is a Lie subalgebra of End(g) under commutator, and ad(g) is an ideal with kernel Z(g).

references.title: Etingof, MIT 18.745 notes, derivations in §3.2

items.title: Semidirect products of Lie algebras
items.statement: Given ρ:g→Der(h), define g⋉_ρ h on g⊕h by [(x,u),(y,v)]=([x,y],ρ(x)v−ρ(y)u+[u,v]).

references.title: Kirillov, An Introduction to Lie Groups and Lie Algebras, semidirect-product convention in §3.3

items.title: The semidirect-product bracket satisfies Jacobi
items.statement: The bracket in g⋉_ρh is bilinear, alternating, and satisfies Jacobi.

references.title: Kirillov, An Introduction to Lie Groups and Lie Algebras, semidirect products in §3.3

items.title: Representations of Lie algebras
items.statement: A representation of g on V is a Lie-algebra homomorphism ρ:g→gl(V), equivalently a bilinear action with [x,y]v=x(yv)−y(xv).

references.title: Etingof, MIT 18.745 notes, §11.1, printed pp. 61–62
Kirillov, An Introduction to Lie Groups and Lie Algebras, §4.1, printed pp. 49–50

items.title: Subrepresentations, quotient representations, and intertwiners
items.statement: A stable subspace W⊆V is a subrepresentation; V/W has x(v+W)=xv+W; an intertwiner commutes with every x-action.

references.title: Etingof, MIT 18.745 notes, §11.1, printed pp. 61–62
Kirillov, An Introduction to Lie Groups and Lie Algebras, §4.1, printed pp. 49–50

items.title: Irreducible, completely reducible, and faithful representations
items.statement: A nonzero representation is irreducible if its only stable subspaces are 0,V; completely reducible if it is a direct sum of irreducibles; faithful if ρ is injective.

references.title: Etingof, MIT 18.745 notes, §11.1, printed pp. 61–62
Kirillov, An Introduction to Lie Groups and Lie Algebras, §4.3, printed pp. 52–53

items.title: Representation kernels are ideals
items.statement: The kernel of ρ:g→gl(V) is an ideal and the representation is faithful exactly when this kernel is zero.

references.title: Kirillov, An Introduction to Lie Groups and Lie Algebras, §4.1, printed pp. 49–50

items.title: Direct-sum, dual, Hom, and tensor representations
items.statement: Representations induce actions x(v_i)=(xv_i), (xλ)(v)=−λ(xv), (xT)(v)=xT(v)−T(xv), and x(v⊗w)=xv⊗w+v⊗xw.

references.title: Etingof, MIT 18.745 notes, §11.2, printed pp. 62–63
Kirillov, An Introduction to Lie Groups and Lie Algebras, §4.2, printed pp. 50–52

items.title: Symmetric and exterior powers over an arbitrary field
items.statement: For n≥0, S^n(V) is V^{⊗n} modulo the span of t−σt for permutations σ, while Λ^n(V) is the repeated-vector quotient of the published exterior-power definition. Neither construction divides by n!.

references.title: Etingof, MIT 18.745 notes, §11.2, printed pp. 62–63

items.title: Symmetric and exterior powers are representations
items.statement: The diagonal tensor action preserves the symmetry and alternating relation subspaces, so it descends to S^nV and Λ^nV.

references.title: Etingof, MIT 18.745 notes, §11.2, printed pp. 62–63

items.title: Lie representations as actions before enveloping
items.statement: A representation is equivalently a k-bilinear action satisfying [x,y]v=x(yv)−y(xv); in general the action does not make g an associative unital ring with V as module. The zero-ring/zero-module case is an exception.

references.title: Etingof, MIT 18.745 notes, §11.1, printed pp. 61–62
Kirillov, An Introduction to Lie Groups and Lie Algebras, §4.1, printed pp. 49–50

items.title: Tensor algebra of a vector space
items.statement: T(V)=⊕_{n≥0}V^{⊗n}, with V^{⊗0}=k, and multiplication by concatenation through tensor associativity.

references.title: Etingof, MIT 18.745 notes, §12.1, printed pp. 69–70
Kirillov, An Introduction to Lie Groups and Lie Algebras, §5.1, printed pp. 71–72

items.title: Universal property of the tensor algebra
items.statement: Every linear f:V→A into a unital associative k-algebra extends uniquely to a unital algebra homomorphism T(V)→A.

references.title: Etingof, MIT 18.745 notes, §12.1, printed pp. 69–70
Kirillov, An Introduction to Lie Groups and Lie Algebras, §5.1, printed pp. 71–72

items.title: Symmetric algebra of a vector space
items.statement: S(V) is T(V) modulo the two-sided ideal generated by v⊗w−w⊗v.

references.title: Etingof, MIT 18.745 notes, §13.1, printed pp. 74–75

items.title: Universal property of the symmetric algebra
items.statement: Every linear map V→A into a commutative unital k-algebra extends uniquely to a unital algebra homomorphism S(V)→A.

references.title: Etingof, MIT 18.745 notes, §13.1, printed pp. 74–75

items.title: Universal enveloping algebra
items.statement: U(g)=T(g)/I where I is generated by x⊗y−y⊗x−[x,y]; write ι:g→U(g) for the composite of the degree-one inclusion and quotient. No injectivity is asserted here.

references.title: Etingof, MIT 18.745 notes, §12.1, printed pp. 69–70
Kirillov, An Introduction to Lie Groups and Lie Algebras, §5.1, printed pp. 71–72

items.title: The canonical map to U(g) is a Lie homomorphism
items.statement: The map ι:g→U(g) satisfies ι([x,y])=ι(x)ι(y)−ι(y)ι(x).

references.title: Etingof, MIT 18.745 notes, §12.1, printed pp. 69–70
Kirillov, An Introduction to Lie Groups and Lie Algebras, §5.1, printed pp. 71–72

items.title: Universal property of the enveloping algebra
items.statement: If f:g→A_Lie is a Lie homomorphism into the commutator Lie algebra of a unital associative k-algebra A, there is a unique unital algebra homomorphism f̄:U(g)→A with f̄ι=f.

references.title: Etingof, MIT 18.745 notes, §12.1, printed pp. 69–70
Kirillov, An Introduction to Lie Groups and Lie Algebras, §5.1, printed pp. 71–72

items.title: Lie representations are U(g)-modules
items.statement: Restriction along ι and extension by the universal property give mutually inverse correspondences between representations of g and unital left U(g)-module structures whose k-scalar action agrees with that on V; the correspondence preserves intertwiners.

references.title: Etingof, MIT 18.745 notes, §12.1, printed pp. 69–70
Kirillov, An Introduction to Lie Groups and Lie Algebras, Theorem 5.2, printed pp. 71–72

items.title: Functoriality of the enveloping algebra
items.statement: A Lie homomorphism f:g→h induces a unique unital algebra homomorphism U(f):U(g)→U(h), and U preserves identities and composition.

references.title: Etingof, MIT 18.745 notes, §12.1, printed pp. 69–70

items.title: PBW filtration on the enveloping algebra
items.statement: F_nU(g) is the image in U(g) of tensors of degree at most n, with F_{−1}=0.

references.title: Etingof, MIT 18.745 notes, §§12.2 and 13.1, printed pp. 70 and 74–75
Kirillov, An Introduction to Lie Groups and Lie Algebras, §5.2, printed pp. 72–74

items.title: Associated graded algebra of a filtered algebra
items.statement: For an increasing multiplicative filtration F_{−1}=0⊆F_0⊆…, define gr_F A=⊕_{n≥0}F_n/F_{n−1}, with (a+F_{m−1})(b+F_{n−1})=ab+F_{m+n−1}.

references.title: Etingof, MIT 18.745 notes, §12.2, printed p. 70

items.title: The PBW filtration is multiplicative and has commutative associated graded
items.statement: F_mF_n⊆F_{m+n}; moreover commutators lower degree by one, so gr U(g) is commutative.

references.title: Etingof, MIT 18.745 notes, §§12.2 and 13.1, printed pp. 70 and 74–75
Kirillov, An Introduction to Lie Groups and Lie Algebras, §5.2, printed pp. 72–74

items.title: PBW symbol map from the symmetric algebra
items.statement: The commuting degree-one symbols define a graded algebra map σ:S(g)→gr U(g).

references.title: Etingof, MIT 18.745 notes, §13.1, printed pp. 74–75

items.title: Ordered monomial basis of a symmetric algebra
items.statement: If B is a basis of V equipped with a total order, the finite weakly increasing words in B, including the empty word, form a basis of S(V).

references.title: Etingof, MIT 18.745 notes, §13.1, printed pp. 74–75

items.title: PBW spanning by ordered monomials
items.statement: If B is a basis of g equipped with a total order, then weakly increasing finite monomials in B span U(g).

references.title: Etingof, MIT 18.745 notes, §13.1, printed pp. 74–75
Kirillov, An Introduction to Lie Groups and Lie Algebras, Lemma 5.10, printed pp. 73–74

items.title: PBW linear independence via the ordered-monomial model
items.statement: For a basis B with a total order, the ordered monomials in U(g) are linearly independent.

references.title: Pavel Etingof, MIT 18.745 Lie Groups and Lie Algebras I
references.locator: Lemma 13.11 and its complete adjacent-transposition/Jacobi proof, printed pages 75–77

references.title: Alexander Kirillov Jr., An Introduction to Lie Groups and Lie Algebras
references.locator: Theorem 5.11 and the regular-representation proof outline, printed page 74

items.title: Poincaré–Birkhoff–Witt theorem
items.statement: For any Lie algebra g and any supplied basis B equipped with a total order, weakly increasing monomials in B form a basis of U(g); equivalently σ:S(g)→gr U(g) is a graded-algebra isomorphism.

references.title: Pavel Etingof, MIT 18.745 Lie Groups and Lie Algebras I
references.locator: Theorems 13.1–13.2 and Lemma 13.11 with complete proof, printed pages 74–77

references.title: Alexander Kirillov Jr., An Introduction to Lie Groups and Lie Algebras
references.locator: Theorems 5.11–5.12 and surrounding discussion, printed pages 74–75

items.title: The canonical map g→U(g) is injective
items.statement: For every Lie algebra g, the canonical map ι:g→U(g) is injective whenever a basis of g is supplied; in particular no degree-one basis vector vanishes.

references.title: Etingof, MIT 18.745 notes, Corollary 13.3, printed p. 75
Kirillov, An Introduction to Lie Groups and Lie Algebras, Corollary 5.13, printed p. 75

items.title: No hidden linear relations in degree one
items.statement: The natural map k⊕g→F_1U(g), (a,x)↦a1+ι(x), is an isomorphism when a basis of g is supplied.

references.title: Etingof, MIT 18.745 notes, Theorem 13.1 and Corollary 13.3, printed pp. 74–75

items.title: PBW symmetrization in characteristic zero
items.statement: If char(k)=0 and a basis of g is supplied, sym:S(g)→U(g), v_1…v_n↦(1/n!)Σ_{π∈S_n}ι(v_{π1})…ι(v_{πn}), is a filtered vector-space isomorphism, generally not an algebra map.

references.title: Etingof, MIT 18.745 notes, Corollary 13.7, printed p. 75
Kirillov, An Introduction to Lie Groups and Lie Algebras, Corollary 5.15, printed p. 75

items.title: The enveloping algebra of an abelian Lie algebra is symmetric
items.statement: If g is abelian, the canonical algebra map S(g)→U(g) is an isomorphism.

references.title: Etingof, MIT 18.745 notes, Example 12.2, printed p. 69
Kirillov, An Introduction to Lie Groups and Lie Algebras, §5.1, printed pp. 71–72

items.title: Enveloping algebra of a direct sum
items.statement: For Lie algebras g,h, U(g⊕h)≅U(g)⊗_kU(h) as unital algebras.

references.title: Etingof, MIT 18.745 notes, enveloping universal property in §12.1, printed pp. 69–70

items.title: Schur’s lemma for irreducible Lie-algebra representations
items.statement: A nonzero intertwiner between irreducible g-representations is an isomorphism; the endomorphism ring of an irreducible representation is a division ring. Over an algebraically closed field, scalarity requires the usual finite-dimensional hypothesis.

references.title: Etingof, MIT 18.745 notes, §11.2, printed pp. 64–65
Kirillov, An Introduction to Lie Groups and Lie Algebras, Theorem 4.29, printed p. 54

items.title: Hopf-algebra structure on U(g)
items.statement: The formulas Δ(x)=x⊗1+1⊗x, ε(x)=0, and S(x)=−x extend to the standard cocommutative Hopf structure on U(g); this remark is non-load-bearing.

references.title: Etingof, MIT 18.745 notes, §12.3, printed pp. 71–72

items.title: Not every Lie subalgebra is an ideal
items.statement: Every Lie subalgebra is an ideal.

references.title: Etingof, MIT 18.745 notes, Lie subalgebras and ideals in §8.3, printed pp. 50–51

items.title: The dual action needs a minus sign
items.statement: The dual action is (xλ)(v)=λ(xv) with no minus sign.

references.title: Etingof, MIT 18.745 notes, dual representations in §11.2, printed pp. 62–63
Kirillov, An Introduction to Lie Groups and Lie Algebras, §4.2, printed pp. 50–52

items.title: An enveloping algebra need not be commutative
items.statement: U(g) is commutative for every Lie algebra g.

references.title: Etingof, MIT 18.745 notes, §§12.1 and 13.1, printed pp. 69–70 and 74–75

items.title: Injectivity is not part of the enveloping quotient definition
items.statement: The canonical map g→U(g) is injective merely by the definition of U(g) as a quotient.

references.title: Etingof, MIT 18.745 notes, Corollary 13.3, printed p. 75

items.title: PBW symmetrization is generally not multiplicative
items.statement: For nonabelian g in characteristic zero, PBW symmetrization S(g)→U(g) is an algebra isomorphism.

references.title: Etingof, MIT 18.745 notes, Corollary 13.7, printed p. 75

items.title: Lie-algebra representations need not be completely reducible
items.statement: Every representation of every Lie algebra is completely reducible.

references.title: Kirillov, An Introduction to Lie Groups and Lie Algebras, §4.3, printed pp. 52–53

title: Lie Algebra Representations Enveloping Algebras and Pbw — Examples

items.title: Adjoint and trivial representations
items.statement: Every Lie algebra acts on itself by ad_x(y)=[x,y], and acts trivially on any vector space by zero operators.

references.title: Etingof, MIT 18.745 notes, Example 11.1, printed p. 62
Kirillov, An Introduction to Lie Groups and Lie Algebras, Examples 4.2–4.3, printed p. 49

items.title: Standard representations of classical matrix Lie algebras
items.statement: Matrix Lie algebras gl_n, sl_n, so_n, and sp_{2n} act on their defining vector spaces by matrix multiplication.

references.title: Etingof, MIT 18.745 notes, Examples 11.1 and classical groups in §6, printed pp. 38–44 and 62
Kirillov, An Introduction to Lie Groups and Lie Algebras, §4.1, printed pp. 49–50

items.title: A semidirect-product Lie algebra from a linear action
items.statement: A representation ρ:g→gl(V) makes g⋉V a Lie algebra with V an abelian ideal.

references.title: Kirillov, An Introduction to Lie Groups and Lie Algebras, semidirect products in §3.3 and representations in §4.1

items.title: The affine Lie algebra as a semidirect product
items.statement: The Lie algebra of affine transformations of a vector space V is gl(V)⋉V with [(A,u),(B,v)]=([A,B],Av−Bu).

references.title: Kirillov, An Introduction to Lie Groups and Lie Algebras, semidirect products in §3.3

items.title: Tensor, dual, and Hom representation formulas
items.statement: For representations V,W, the actions are x(v⊗w)=xv⊗w+v⊗xw, (xλ)(v)=−λ(xv), and (xT)=x_WT−Tx_V.

references.title: Etingof, MIT 18.745 notes, §11.2, printed pp. 62–63
Kirillov, An Introduction to Lie Groups and Lie Algebras, §4.2, printed pp. 50–52

items.title: The enveloping algebra of a one-dimensional abelian Lie algebra
items.statement: If g=kx is abelian, U(g)≅k[t] by x↦t.

references.title: Etingof, MIT 18.745 notes, Example 12.2, printed p. 69
Kirillov, An Introduction to Lie Groups and Lie Algebras, Example 5.1, printed p. 71

items.title: PBW basis for the Heisenberg Lie algebra
items.statement: For [x,y]=z and z central, the monomials x^a y^b z^c form a basis of U(h) in the order x<y<z.

references.title: Etingof, MIT 18.745 notes, PBW examples in §13.1, printed pp. 74–75
Kirillov, An Introduction to Lie Groups and Lie Algebras, §5.2, printed pp. 72–75

items.title: PBW reordering in sl_2
items.statement: For [h,e]=2e, [h,f]=−2f, [e,f]=h, PBW gives the basis f^a h^b e^c and the relations reorder every word into that form.

references.title: Etingof, MIT 18.745 notes, Example 13.9, printed p. 75
Kirillov, An Introduction to Lie Groups and Lie Algebras, Example 5.14, printed p. 75

items.title: A nonsplit two-dimensional representation
items.statement: Let a one-dimensional abelian Lie algebra act on k² by N(e_2)=e_1, N(e_1)=0. The line ke_1 is invariant but has no invariant complement.

references.title: Kirillov, An Introduction to Lie Groups and Lie Algebras, irreducibility in §4.3, printed pp. 52–53

items.title: Symmetrization does not preserve products in sl_2
items.statement: In sl_2, sym(eh)=1/2(eh+he) differs from sym(e)sym(h)=eh.

references.title: Etingof, MIT 18.745 notes, Corollary 13.7 and Example 13.9, printed p. 75

items.title: Stability under one generator is not enough
items.statement: In the standard sl_2-module k², the highest-weight line is stable under e but not under f, hence is not a subrepresentation.

references.title: Etingof, MIT 18.745 notes, standard sl_2 representation in §11.4, printed pp. 65–69

items.title: The Casimir element in U(sl_2)
items.statement: In characteristic zero, Ω=ef+fe+(1/2)h² is a well-defined element of U(sl_2). Its centrality is not asserted or used on this page.

references.title: Etingof, MIT 18.745 notes, Example 13.9, printed p. 75
Kirillov, An Introduction to Lie Groups and Lie Algebras, Example 5.6, printed p. 73
